title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the streets and corridors immediately surrounding the College of the Holy Cross, from the industrial history of Southbridge Street to the student-frequented eateries of Shrewsbury Street.

cards.title: The Gateway Corridor
cards.subtitle: Southbridge Street
cards.notes: Walk past the former Rotmans Furniture site, a 14-acre landmark recently acquired by the college for future campus expansion and neighborhood revitalization.
cards.short_summary: A major industrial and commercial corridor serving as the primary gateway to the Holy Cross campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Cross and Madison Properties purchased the former Rotmans Furniture property at 725 Southbridge Street to serve the college's core mission.
cards.source_title: Holy Cross and Madison Properties Purchase Former Rotmans Furniture Property in Worcester
cards.access_notes: Public street access; the specific Rotmans site is currently under master planning for future use.

cards.title: The Main Approach
cards.subtitle: College Street
cards.notes: Ascend the hill toward the main gate, passing the Ciocca Center for Business, Ethics and Society located at the base of the campus.
cards.short_summary: The primary residential and academic artery connecting the South Worcester neighborhood to the campus gates.
cards.evidence_claim: The College of the Holy Cross is located at 1 College Street, which serves as the main address and entry point.
cards.source_title: Maps and Directions | College of the Holy Cross
cards.access_notes: Public roadway providing the main vehicular and pedestrian access to the college.

cards.title: The Nature Link
cards.subtitle: McKeon Road
cards.notes: Access the Blackstone Gateway Park from this road, which features a half-mile of accessible boardwalks and bridges over the Middle River.
cards.short_summary: A southern perimeter road that connects the campus to regional recreational trails and the Blackstone River Valley.
cards.evidence_claim: Blackstone Gateway Park connects the Visitor Center to the McKeon Road entrance to the Holy Cross campus.
cards.source_title: Holy Cross Celebrates Opening of Visitors Center and Park Near Campus
cards.access_notes: Public road with direct access to the Blackstone Heritage Corridor Visitor Center.

cards.title: Restaurant Row
cards.subtitle: Shrewsbury Street
cards.notes: Visit this mile-long stretch for student favorites like Volturno for wood-fired pizza or InHouse Coffee for study sessions.
cards.short_summary: Worcester's premier dining destination, located a short drive from campus and popular for student outings.
cards.evidence_claim: Shrewsbury Street is a mile-and-a-half long street home to 32 restaurants and is a favorite off-campus spot for students.
cards.access_notes: Public commercial street; most businesses are open daily with varying hours.

cards.title: Senior Living Block
cards.subtitle: City View Street
cards.notes: Walk past the newly constructed senior-only townhouses that offer apartment-style living on the northern edge of campus.
cards.short_summary: A residential street on the campus periphery recently developed into high-density student housing.
cards.evidence_claim: The Townhouses, located on the corner of City View and College Street, opened in 2023 as a senior-only residence hall.
cards.source_title: Townhouses | College of the Holy Cross
cards.access_notes: Public street; townhouse interiors are restricted to residents and guests.

cards.title: The Cookson Field Entry
cards.subtitle: Kendig Street
cards.notes: Find the entrance to Cookson Field, an 18-acre wooded park that the college and city collaborated to rehabilitate for community use.
cards.short_summary: A quiet residential street providing access to one of the neighborhood's largest undeveloped green spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Cookson Field is located on Kendig Street (off College Street) and consists of approximately 18 acres of wooded space.
cards.source_title: Holy Cross and City Announce Development of Master Plan to Rehabilitate Cookson Field
cards.access_notes: Public street access to the park; park is open dawn to dusk.

cards.title: The South Worcester Hub
cards.subtitle: Cambridge Street
cards.notes: Explore the local businesses and community services in this district, which connects the college to the wider South Worcester area.
cards.short_summary: A major cross-town thoroughfare that serves as a commercial anchor for the neighborhood surrounding the college.
cards.evidence_claim: The South Worcester neighborhood, including the Cambridge Street area, is part of the college's community outreach and planning efforts.
cards.source_title: Worcester & Beyond | College of the Holy Cross
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare with numerous retail and service businesses.

cards.title: The Canal District Edge
cards.subtitle: Millbury Street
cards.notes: Walk toward the Canal District to find the Worcester Public Market and various local eateries popular with the student body.
cards.short_summary: An evolving commercial street that links the college area to the historic and trendy Canal District.
cards.evidence_claim: Students frequent spots like Pasta Mani in the Worcester Public Market, which is located in the nearby Canal District area.
cards.source_title: Favorite Coffee Shops and Local Places to Eat in Worcester
cards.access_notes: Public street; market hours vary by vendor but generally open daily.

cards.title: The Historic Hilltop
cards.subtitle: Pakachoag Street
cards.notes: Visit the Pakachoag Center for Arts, Recreation, Spirituality, and Culture, located just over the town line in Auburn.
cards.short_summary: A historic road on Pakachoag Hill, the original site of the Nipmuc people and the foundation of the college.
cards.evidence_claim: The land was originally known as Pakachoag Hill and is home to the Pakachoag Center at 203 Pakachoag St.
cards.access_notes: Public street; center hours depend on scheduled programs and events.

cards.title: The Urban Village
cards.subtitle: Green Street
cards.notes: Explore the heart of the Canal District, featuring the new Polar Park stadium and a variety of student-friendly cafes like Nu Kitchen.
cards.short_summary: A vibrant urban street known for its revitalization, sports venues, and diverse dining options.
cards.evidence_claim: Nu Cafe (Nu Kitchen) is a crowd pleaser and a go-to off-campus spot for students, located in the Green Street area.
cards.source_title: Favorite Coffee Shops and Local Places to Eat in Worcester
cards.access_notes: Public street; very walkable with high pedestrian activity during game days.
